newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow-Iraq see Qurna field output one mln bpd.
newsitem.headline: Moscow-Iraq see Qurna field output one mln bpd.

text.p: Oil production capacity at Iraq's West Qurna oil field, which will be developed jointly with Russia's LUKoil, could reach one million barrels per day (bpd) in four to six years after work begins, Iraq's ambassador to Russia said on Tuesday.

"Two to three years after concrete work begins, the field will produce 600,000 barrels per day, and after, say, another two to three years, production will reach one million barrels per day," Hassan Fahmi Jumah told a news conference.
Russian companies along with Chinese and French firms are leading the race to tie up oil deals with Iraq, the country which holds the world's second largest oil reserves behind Saudi Arabia.
LUKoil and partners Zarubezhneft and Mashinoimport signed in March to develop 7-8 billion barrels of reserves in the southern Qurna oilfield

Potential output capacity from the field is put at 600,000 barrels a day (bpd) and Iraqi officials have said the companies could win rights to the entire Qurna (Qurana) oilfield region, the officials said.

The whole field is believed by Iraq to hold anywhere between 15 and 30 billion barrels and Iraqi officials say the Russian companies could win rights to the entire southern Iraq Qurna (Qurana) oilfield region.

Iraq has been encouraging potential oil production partners to sign upstream agreements despite a United Nations ban on investment which will postpone the lion's share of any work until sanctions are lifted.
U.N. sanctions imposed after Baghdad's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait ban investment or trade with Iraq.
Moscow has stressed it will not violate U.N. sanctions. Russian officials said only preliminary feasibility and financing work would begin before sanctions ended.

But Iraqi officials say the Russian companies are obliged to spend $200 million during sanctions on "activities related" to Qurna development and extend a $100 million loan to Iraq for the purchase of equipment.
